verdict.reasoning: Patient states reduced hearing in left ear: 'I just feel like I can't really hear as well as I used to... For about six weeks.' and confirms it's 'Just the left ear, yeah.'

'Progressive' deterioration is not stated; patient only says 'I just feel like I can't really hear as well as I used to.' However, intermittent left-sided hearing issue and a prior brief episode a year ago are supported: 'For about six weeks' and 'I had something maybe about a year ago, but it only lasted a couple of days.'
Patient describes intermittent left-sided tinnitus: 'I occasionally get like a ringing in my left ear just on the one side... It's kind of on and off.'

Patient reports mild dizziness/imbalance without true vertigo: 'a few times when I felt kind of a bit sick or a bit dizzy' and later clarifies 'It's not that kind of dizziness you get with nausea, like not proper room spinning or anything like that, but just a little bit kind of off balance.'

Patient notes TV and music trigger symptoms: 'some things trigger it as well. So, for example, if I'm watching TV or listening to music or something. Something that will set off the ringing in the ear.'
The doctor asks: 'And have you had any pain from the ear at all?' but the patient's verbal response is not captured in the transcript, so an explicit denial of ear pain is not documented.
The doctor asks: 'Any discharge coming out of the ear?' but no patient answer is transcribed, so an explicit denial of ear discharge is not documented.

The doctor asks: 'Have you been experiencing any fever?' and patient says: 'Not specifically, apart from the dizziness and sickness I mentioned before.' This is not an explicit denial of fever; the fact stating 'denies fever' overstates what is said.
Patient explicitly denies ear itching: Doctor: 'And has your ear been itchy at all?' Patient: 'No.'
The transcript contains only conversation and plans; there are no recorded physical exam findings or vitals, supporting 'no documented exam findings or vital signs.'

Assessment content matches history: intermittent unilateral left hearing problem for 6 weeks ('For about six weeks... Just the left ear, yeah.'), associated tinnitus ('ringing in my left ear... kind of on and off') and mild imbalance/nausea ('a bit sick or a bit dizzy... not proper room spinning... just a little bit kind of off balance').
Doctor discusses tinnitus as part of assessment: 'Does it seem like the ringing that you've got that you've got something called tinnitus.'

Vestibular-type symptoms are described as mild imbalance without true vertigo: 'not proper room spinning or anything like that, but just a little bit kind of off balance,' which fits the characterization in the assessment.

Doctor plans a face-to-face ear check in 4–5 days, non-emergency, with admin scheduling: 'book you in for a face to face appointment... it can be done within the next four, five days or so... I'll send a message to our admin team, I'll ask them to slot you into one of our clinics in that time frame.'

Otoscopic exam to exclude wax is planned: 'we need to get someone to have a look inside your ear... Simple things might be wax... which can lead to muffled hearing... we need to exclude that first.' While removal is not explicitly stated, exclusion of cerumen impaction as a cause is clearly planned.

Doctor states that if no physical blockage is found, further evaluation of drum and balance system will follow: 'figure out whether there's a physical blockage or whether there's something else going on... It might be that there's a problem inside the drum or the balance system... but we just need to exclude whether there's a physical blockage first.'

Doctor plans to add tinnitus leaflet link to notes: 'I'm going to put paste the link for a leaflet about tinnitus in the notes for this appointment. I'd really appreciate it if you could start reading about it.'

Patient is told to rebook if issues arise: 'If there's any problem, any issues between now and when the clinic appointment is, just book another appointment and you can speak to her and we'll serve a video.'
